raceEventDetails.timeForm: EARTH SHOT has the potential for considerable improvement on the back of her eye-catching debut second and should prove hard to beat for William Haggas. The main threat may come from newcomer Velvet Vega, particularly if the betting vibes are strong given the yard has been mopping up in similar races in recent weeks. Malika is a likely improver for last year's winning owner/trainer.

racers.timeForm: €240,000 Lope de Vega filly. Dam, useful French 1m-9.4f winner, half-sister to useful 7f-9.5f winner Lucie Manette. A very interesting debutante for a leading stable in very good form.
2501/, last of 9 in 7f Southwell novice on debut for Lawrence Mullaney last autumn. Big outsider again on return for new stable.
15/2, showed ability when fourth of 12 in maiden at Leicester (7f, good) on debut last October. Steps up 3f in trip on return. Should progress.
20/1 when well-held fourth of 13 in maiden at Kempton (1m) on debut in November. Didn't achieve much on that occasion but she's open to improvement for last year's winning owner/trainer.
Zarak filly. Dam 2-y-o 7f winner. The betting should help guide to expectations.
125/1 when well held on 1m Yarmouth debut 20 days ago, very slowly away.

Highly promising debut when 2 lengths second of 9 in novice at Newbury (1m, heavy) on debut, finishing full of running behind a stable-companion. This longer trip is sure to suit. Likely hard to beat.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: Charlie Appleby has won this 5 times since 2016 and POSEIDON'S WARRIOR should take a bit of stopping on the back of his promising second in the Feilden. My Love Is King has made a highly encouraging start to his career and can give Godolphin's charge most to do.

racers.timeForm: Fetched 1,100,000 gns as a yearling and won novices at Beverley (7.5f) and Goodwood (1m) on good to firm last summer. Something possibly not right when 14 lengths seventh of 8 to Bow Echo in Royal Lodge over 1m here in the autumn. Retains potential.

Kingman colt who was a cosy winner of a 7f Newcastle novice on debut last November. Useful effort when narrowly denied in 1¼m Newbury novice (good) on return a fortnight ago. Looks sure to progress again for leading stable enjoying a fine spring.
425,000 gns Wootton Bassett colt who confirmed his debut promise when landing the odds in a 1m course maiden (good) last autumn. Useful prospect.

Winner of both starts since joining Marco Botti, latterly showing useful form in a C&D handicap at last month's Craven meeting. More needed in a higher grade now but further progress isn't discounted.

Goodwood novice winner last autumn and produced a near-smart effort when length second of 7 to Morshdi in listed Feilden on 9f course reappearance 16 days ago. Today's slightly longer trip should play to his strengths. Hood goes on and hard to beat for a yard with a strong record in this.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: A good 3-y-o handicap. LAKE COMO shaped well behind 2000 Guineas contender King's Trail in a Kempton conditions race last time and could be well treated back in a handicap. Unbeaten pair Fort Rock and Zennor Storm should have more to offer now moving into their first handicaps, while St Anton showed he can be very competitive from his mark when third at the Craven meeting.

racers.timeForm: Ready winner of 7.5f Beverley novice (good to firm) last summer. Excuses when well beaten in the Group 2 Vintage at Goodwood on his final 2-y-o start and resumed his progression when length second of 6 on 1m Musselburgh reappearance 27 days ago. Appeals as one who can carry on improving.

Has proved a revelation for new yard (purchased for 16,000 gns following debut for Aidan O'Brien), winning novice/handicap on all-weather in December. Improved again when third of 9 to 2000 Guineas candidate King's Trail in conditions race at Kempton (1m) in March. Of firm interest back in handicap.
Ended 2025 with a pair of all-weather handicap wins but his mark went up a combined 15 lb and there's a suspicion he could be vulnerable to some of the many progressive sorts in this line up.

Looked useful when going 2-2 in novices over 8.5f at Wolverhampton around the turn of the year. Switches to turf for his handicap debut after 98 days off.  Another in this field who should have more to offer.
Mohaather colt who won a 7f maiden and 1m novice on Kempton's all-weather towards the end of 2025. Makes handicap and turf debut on return. Useful prospect.
Made it fourth time lucky when landing the odds in 7f Kempton novice in February. Beaten favourite in 1m Musselburgh handicap (good to soft) over Easter but it's still early days for leading stable.
Won a 1m Kempton nursery at the end of last summer but beaten twice off this mark in the autumn and looks vulnerable up against less-exposed sorts on reappearance. Has been gelded.
Wootton Bassett colt who was a narrow winner of a pair of 7f Kempton novices last autumn. The runner-up in those races have boosted the form since. Very useful prospect for top yard.
Still a maiden but has improved with every start, keeping on for a promising third of 12 on C&D handicap debut/reappearance 17 days ago. Likely to be in the thick of things from an unchanged mark.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: BAY CITY ROLLER has a near miss in a Group 2 and win in a Group 1 to show from his previous outings over 1½m and is selected to make light of a penalty on his return to action. Second choice is Sunway, who can be excused his latest run in Dubai and had been in good form there prior to that. Lion's Pride is also respected back at the scene of his easy listed success last autumn.

racers.timeForm: Smart handicapper who has been a tremendous servant for connections and looked as good as ever when winning at Lingfield (1½m) in February. Creditable third of 14 at Newcastle (1¼m) on Good Friday but more will be needed now tackling a pattern race for first time back on turf.

Emphatic winner of a C&D listed race last autumn. Found out at Group 2 level in the Middle East over the winter but made a respectable return to Britain when 3½ lengths fourth of 6 to Convergent in the John Porter at Newbury (1½m, good) 13 days ago.

Winner of 1¾m handicaps at Goodwood and Royal Ascot at the start of last summer. Weakened quickly in the Ebor on final start but his yard's good form provides hope that he may bounce back on return (has been gelded). Goes without the headgear he wore on final 3 starts last year.

Fourth in the 2022 2000 Guineas here. Off for 2 years after that but still capable of smart form, winning Newbury Group 3 and Milan Group 2 over this trip last season. Well beaten in Hong Kong on final start.

Runner-up in 3 Group 2s in France last season before easily winning a soft-ground Group 1 at Munich (1½m) on his final 3-y-o start. That very smart performance gives him leading form claims here, even under a 3 lb penalty.

Progressed very well last year, winning 4 times, including the Group 2 Park Hill at Doncaster (1¾m, good). Respectable 4½ lengths second of 12 to Consent in Group 1 Prix de Royallieu at Longchamp (1¾m, good to soft) on final start.

Generally reliable type who started the year with a win and second in Group 3s over 1¾m at Meydan. Too keen in blinkers when well beaten in the 2m Dubai Gold Cup there 5 weeks ago. The blinkers are left off on his return to Britain. Could bounce back with a bang.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: Andrew Balding bagged this prize 12 months ago and looks to have another prime candidate in the shape of GOLDEN REDEMPTION. Having ended last season with a pair of solid placed efforts, he promises to be all the better for his reappearance Kempton third and can come out on top. A return to forcing tactics can see C&D winner Elarak in a better light and he's feared most ahead of Silver Ghost and Billyjoh.

racers.timeForm: On a lengthy losing run but boasts some strong form in top-end 6/7f handicaps over the last 2 seasons. Produced a somewhat typical performance when keeping on for eighth in valuable handicap at York (7f) on final outing last year but assessor has eased his grip ahead of return.

Kingman gelding who registered a third success of a productive 2025 in a C&D handicap in September, looking well suited by an aggressive ride back down in trip. Gelded thereafter and entitled to strip fitter for last month's reappearance fourth at Thirsk.

Smart form at best in France, winning 2 of his 3 starts as a 2-y-o, including a Group 3. Lost his way during 2025 but joined a yard (acquired for €37,000) boasting a good record with similar recruits and interesting what the market makes of him. Has been gelded.

Generally had a good winter on the all-weather, winning a handicap at Newcastle (7f) in February and shaped as if still in good form when fifth at Musselburgh (7f) 5 days ago, caught further back than ideal. This is tougher back up in grade, however.

Son of Sea The Stars who finished runner up first 3 starts prior to completing simple task in 6-runner all-weather novice in autumn 2024. Missed whole of last year (had breathing operation/gelded in interim) but goes handicapping with yard amongst the winners. Betting can guide.

Much improved when landing back-to-back 7f handicaps last spring, including over C&D. Acquitted herself with credit thereafter, doing all she could on the far side when sixth behind reopposing Elarak over C&D on final outing. Mark has eased a little more.

Quick to find his feet for Andrew Balding last summer, winning a Newbury maiden (6f) in August. Very good placed efforts in handicaps next 2 starts and made a satisfactory return without being seen to ideal effect when third at Kempton (7f) 5 weeks ago. One to be interested in.

Successful over this trip on July course last year and shaped better than bare result on occasions thereafter. Easy to back and may have needed last month's Thirsk reappearance but he is becoming the type that needs things to fall just right.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: STELLAR SUNRISE quickened up smartly to land what promises to be an informative 3-y-o handicap on return at Newbury 17 days ago and, well worth his place back at a higher level on that evidence, he earns the vote. Well-bred debut winners Saber Strike and Cerro Blanco both hail from leading stables also and may emerge as the dangers.

racers.timeForm: Third in a 6f Group 2 on July course last summer and landed a valuable sales race over C&D on final start, benefiting from increased emphasis on stamina. May have needed run after 6 months off when fourth in listed company at Newcastle (1m) 4 weeks ago and fancied to take a step forward here.

Night of Thunder colt who hails from a useful family and proved a class apart from his rivals when running out a 3-length winner of a Redcar novice (6f) on debut in November. Takes a marked step up in class on return but in top hands and there's surely plenty more to come.

Won in big fields at 2 of the summer festivals as a juvenile and away from very testing ground, got back on the up in no uncertain terms after 4 months off when landing an informative 3-y-o handicap at Newbury (7f) 2 weeks ago, quickening up smartly. Well worth his place back at this higher level.

Invincible Army filly who opened her account at third attempt at Southwell (7f) in January. Stepped up further in defeat, runner up in 1m conditions event prior to finishing fourth in Group 3 Fred Darling at Newbury 2 weeks ago.

Landed first 2 starts as a 2-y-o, including Woodcote at Epsom. Failed to make an impact in pair of Group 2s after but confirmed he's capable of useful form when twice placed in Meydan earlier this year. Just similar form when third in C&D conditions event latest and he's more exposed than some.

Wootton Bassett colt who overcame inexperience and justified cramped odds in the process when making a winning debut in a C&D maiden 17 days ago. Well on top at the finish and this imposing sort looks well worth his place at this higher level.

gameStateTimeScore.gameEventComments: We are paying 4 PLACES instead of 3 at 1/5 odds (min 12). BOG does not apply to Each Way bets. T&C's apply.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: Having been progressive last year, LADY ROXBY shaped as if as good as ever when third on her recent Kempton return and with that outing under her belt, Michael Herrington's 4-y-o gets the nod to regain the winning thread. Paradise Walk has found one too good on all 3 starts so far and she may have to settle for silver once again, with Angel Love and Cuban Lady another couple to consider in an open-looking sprint to close the card.

racers.timeForm: Progressive last summer, landing novice at Newbury in August before following up in a Goodwood nursery the following month. Too free tried over 7f when down the field in listed company at Newbury (7f) on final outing last season so no surprise to see her back sprinting.

Night of Thunder filly who looked a useful prospect when scoring on debut at Haydock (6f) last September. Down markedly in grade but found her opening mark beyond her on nursery/all-weather debut when third of 4 at Lingfield in November but it remains very early days.

Improved for the switch to current yard last season, scoring at Beverley in July and runner-up on 4 of her 5 other starts, including when just touched off in valuable fillies handicap over C&D last September. Looked as good as ever when third of 7 at Kempton on return so can feature.

Recorded a ninth career success when making all on the July course last summer. Probably needed the run after 5 months off at Wolverhampton in March and she's not out of things from her lower turf mark.

2-2 in all-weather novices to start her career but has still looked rough around the edges in handicaps, shaping as if better for the run after 6 months off at Southwell recently. Handicapper drops her another 2 lb and she's not ruled out back on turf.

Found one too good on all 3 starts, latest in 8-runner novice after 12 weeks off at Wolverhampton in March. In the right hands on handicap/turf debut and she should be a factor in first-time blinkers.

Course winner who wasted no time getting back to form returned to calmer waters when third of 8 at Southwell (6f) 16 days ago, despite having not been seen to best effect behind a pair of improving 3-y-os. Back on turf and fancied to find a few unexposed types too strong.

Promising Harry Angel filly who was a strong favourite and justified the support emphatically in 9-runner maiden at Wolverhampton (6f, 4/5) back in November. Open to further improvement now stepping into handicaps on turf debut.

Made it third time lucky at Windsor last June and not beaten far in 4 subsequent starts, just finding things a little tougher away from her own sex on her final 2025 outing. Plenty to like with Murphy booked for this reappearance.

Bagged a 6f Ripon listed event at the end of last summer but it didn't require any more than a fairly useful effort and she struggled in her 3 subsequent starts. Not beaten far on her recent return to action at Pontefract but may need to head up in trip to find another jolt of progress.

Dual winner on the all-weather but has finished no better than mid-field in a handful of turf starts, fourth of 8 in handicap at this course (7f, good) when last seen in October. Back sprinting for her return but others more appealing.

Ought to have landed a third career success on the July course last June (when reportedly struck into), just failing having been left with plenty to do. Caught wide and ran below form after 9 months at Kempton recently so will need to leave that effort well behind.

Landed a couple of ordinary novices at Chelmsford last year and wasn't good enough returning from 6 months off when fifth of 7 in minor event at Wolverhampton (6f) 3 weeks ago. Hopes pinned on a switch to handicaps bringing out further progress.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: Just a quartet line up for this 2-y-o event but it is one of the more interesting early season juvenile races. ADAAY OF SCARLETT created an excellent impression at Newmarket and gets the nod to follow up. Dance A Jig was unlucky not to score in the Brocklesby and has a good chance of reversing form at the weights with A Bear Affair.

racers.timeForm: Mehmas colt who was impressive when making a winning debut 5-runner novice at Newmarket (5f) 17 days ago. Readily got the better of a subsequent winner then and there's even better to come.

68,000 gns yearling, Kodi Bear colt. Knew what was required when providing his trainer with a third Brocklesby in 5 years in March, finishing ahead of Dance A Jig. Gives weight to that rival this time but he looks sure to progress and win more races.

Naval Crown colt. Shaped very well amidst greenness when ¾-length second of 15 to A Bear Affair in Brocklesby Stakes at Doncaster (5f, good to soft, 6/1) on debut in March, meeting significant in-running trouble. Is better off at the weights with that rival and is a big player.
Acclamation colt who showed ability amidst greenness when fifth of 9 in maiden (16/1) at Newbury (5f, good) on debut 14 days ago. Is in at the deep end but should have more to offer.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: The first 3 from last year's Middle Park meet again in this Group 3 but there's a chance they may be caught cold on their return by GHOST MODE, who scored in impressive fashion on his handicap debut last time and is unexposed at this trip. Brussels may have to settle for another runner-up spot ahead of his Newmarket conqueror Wise Approach.

racers.timeForm: Debut winner at the Curragh last year. Proved expensive to follow after, finishing runner-up on 4 occasions, including twice at the highest level. However, gets a 4 Ib pull at the weights with Wise Approach on their Middle Park meeting and has to be taken seriously.

Hamilton maiden winner who showed fairly useful form twice fourth pair of Group contests here and Newmarket last year. Was amiss on final start in Oh So Sharp Stakes at Newmarket (7f, good to firm). This is a tough ask against the boys on return.

Created a good impression when winning first 2 starts at Wolverhampton. Lost his unbeaten record but wasn't disgraced when fifth in Prix Djebel at Deauville (7f, good, 42/10) 24 days ago. Drops down to 6f and is fitted with a first-time tongue strap. Interesting runner for a yard going well.

Smart colt who won 3 times in 2025, emulating his half-brother Perfect Power in winning the Middle Park Stakes at Newmarket (6f), showing a willing attitude after nearly coming down at the start. Has a penalty to carry but he's a serious player on first start as a 3-y-o.

Had a busy juvenile season, gaining his fifth win in a valuable listed event at Redcar (6f, good to soft) in October prior to finishing second over C&D on Champions Day next start. Ran below form in Greenham Stakes at Newbury (7f, good, 14/1) on return and may find a few too good.

A useful juvenile who improved appreciably on Leicester debut success when third of 20 in Coventry Stakes at Royal Ascot. Stepped up again to win Richmond at Goodwood, seen to good effect from the front. Ran a cracker when third in the Middle Park on latest outing and warrants respect on return.

Recorded a hat-trick last year, winning 2 novice events and a listed race at York (6f). Respectable fifth of 11 in Champions Day Two-Year-Old Conditions Stakes over C&D (good to firm, 10/3) in October but needs a step forward to feature.

Raced mainly at 7f last year, winning a maiden at Chester before being collared late on in a sales race at York. Was much improved when winning 8-runner event on handicap debut at Southwell back at 6f in March. Unexposed as a sprinter and looks worth his place in this.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: REMMOOZ was unraced at 2 yrs but made good strides last year and there could be more to come from this well-bred colt in the months ahead. He shades preference ahead of Bowmark, who represents last year's winning yard and may well start to fulfil his earlier promise having been gelded. La Botte failed to land a blow in the Lincoln but caught the eye in the trial for that race and merits respect, along with Bowmark's stablemate Chancellor, Group 2 winner Jonquil and the consistent Holloway Boy.

racers.timeForm: Returned a much-improved performer following gelding and breathing operations during the winter, winning twice (including listed race at Southwell) and latest fifth of 14 in a valuable Newcastle handicap (1m) was another solid effort. High on the shortlist.

Unlucky second in last year's Britannia at the Royal meeting and eye-catching return to action when fourth in the Lincoln Trial at Wolverhampton. Failed to make an impact in the Lincoln itself but conditions were perhaps against him (good to soft) and he remains of interest.

Debut winner for Sir Michael Stoute and improved to land the Greenham on first run for Andrew Balding last spring before going close in the French 2000 Guineas. Added a Goodwood Group 2 to his CV last summer and, though below par at Abu Dhabi earlier this year, he will be a big player if on-song.

Smart performer who notched first success in pattern company when gamely seeing off 10 rivals in a listed race at Goodwood (1¼m, good) in September. Likely to pay his way again this year but entitled to come on for the run following 7 months off and, moreover, dropping to 1m may not be ideal.

Appeared to be going places when readily landing the odds in 1m York novice last spring, but failed to settle in the French Derby next time and his exuberance again got the better of him back on the Knavesmire in August. However, gelded since and it would be no surprise were he to get back on track.

Went close in a couple of French Group 1s following big-priced success in the Coventry at the Royal meeting here in 2024. Made the frame on several occasions last season and solid each-way chance if ready to roll following a 6-month absence.

Winner of 1m Newmarket maiden on second of his 2 starts as a juvenile and shaped really well on first run since (missed whole of 2025) when third in a 7f conditions race at Thirsk. Return to this trip will be in his favour but a jolt of improvement is needed now upped in class.

Smart and consistent type who got his head back in front when proving a neck too strong for the re-opposing Chancellor in a listed contest at Kempton (1m) in December. Has remained in good heart since, third in a Meydan Group 2 last time, and merits respect with William Buick again booked.

Yet to put a foot wrong in his 6-race career, with his 2 defeats coming in the Jersey Stakes at the Royal meeting here last summer and in a big York handicap in August. Signed off 2025 with a listed success at Newbury (7f, good to soft) and he appeals as the type to kick on again this season.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: ARTAGNAN shaped as if as good as ever when second at Wolverhampton on his return, form which has been boosted since, and he is taken to resume winning ways with his recent run behind him. He gets the vote ahead of Lethal Nymph, who could also take a step forward from his reappearance, with Duran and Hockney completing the shortlist.

racers.timeForm: Making third start for current yard, ran up to best dropped back to 6f when runner-up at Chelmsford in February. Not in the same form when sixth of 8 at Kempton last time, but he looks worth a try at the minimum trip given his free-going nature.

Sole handicap success came at Windsor (6f) last spring. Making first run since leaving Alice Haynes, made a sound seasonal/stable debut when ¾-length third of 6 at Southwell (5f) 22 days ago and he's been eased another 1 lb in the weights.

Dropped back to 5f, doubled her tally when finding plenty to lead close home at Newcastle in March. Backed up that effort returned to turf when second of 6 at Yarmouth 20 days ago, faring best of those held up.

Positive start in handicaps last season, making it 2 wins from 4 outings when scoring at Chepstow in June. Runner-up 4 times later in the campaign, including over this C&D in September, before not handling the turns of Lingfield when last seen 6 months ago.

Runner-up in this race last year before going one better at Haydock next time. Without a win since but made the frame on several occasions and shaped as if better for the run when mid-field at Beverley on return 16 days ago. Enters calculations.

Added to a good record fresh when making a winning stable debut at Newmarket last summer. However, he developed an all-or-nothing profile the remainder of the campaign, last of 14 at Chelmsford on final outing in December.

Continues to go from strength to strength, recording his seventh win in 9 starts at Kempton in February. Ran well in defeat when second at Chelmsford last time, the winner successful twice since, but needs to transfer his progress to turf (well held only previous outing).

Much improved switched to handicap company (following a breathing operation) last autumn, making it back-to-back wins when scoring at Thirsk (6f, soft) in September. Probably needed the run after 6 months off at Newcastle in March, so he remains with potential.

Ended a losing run of almost 4 years when shading a tight finish at Southwell in January. Excuses next time, before respectable fourth of 8 at Newmarket 17 days ago. However, he's still yet to win a turf handicap.

Fitted with tongue strap, got back on the up for current yard when sharing the spoils at Chelmsford (6f) in October. Good efforts both starts since, returning from 5 months off when runner-up at Wolverhampton 22 days ago. Effective on turf and he's a major player.

Successful twice last year, with latest success at Newcastle in November. After 12 weeks off, caught wide in a competitive early-season sprint when sixth of 13 at Pontefract 24 days ago and he can make his presence felt with Colin Keane an interesting jockey booking.

Successful 5 times on all-weather during the autumn/winter, including back-to-back 5f victories at Southwell in January. Good second at the same C&D in March, before a lesser effort at Wolverhampton on latest outing.

Scored twice over 6f on all-weather last June and ended the year with a string of in-frame efforts. After 3 months off, caught wide when down the field at Lingfield in April and he should strip fitter for the run, with usual blinkers now replacing the visor.

Has been in good form at Wolverhampton, making it back-to-back wins with success in January. Good second next time, before suffering trouble in running when last of 5 on his latest outing in February. Needs to prove his effectiveness on turf, though.

Regular slow starter who opened account at Salisbury (6f) last summer. Good efforts when runner-up in 3 subsequent outings last season and he could get the race run to suit dropped back in trip on his return, with good-value claimer on board.

Showed improved form sent handicapping in 2025, winning twice over 6f during the summer including the Brighton Bullet. After a couple of lesser efforts, settled better when fourth of 8 at Chelmsford (5f) in December and he's in good hands to do better still this year.

Winless since his debut when trained by Kevin Ryan and more miss than hit for present stable last summer, well held at Thirsk when last seen in August. Mark has eased further but others more persuasive on return from 8 months off.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: Saytarr will no doubt prove popular having yet to taste defeat in 3 starts for current connections but it could be worth taking a chance on COLOMBIER, who looks on a good opening mark judged on the pick of his French form and has joined a yard that's going well. Recent winners Tilted Kilt and Angel Hunter can do battle for minor honours.

racers.timeForm: Thriving for new yard, completing the hat-trick in 12-runner handicap at Newcastle (1m) 5 weeks ago, the strong pace assisting with how easily he got into contention. Up just 4 lb for his latest success and will be a danger to all if translating that form to the turf.

Improved again to complete Newcastle hat-trick last year. Shaped as if retaining ability first 2 starts over winter but has underperformed the last twice, most recently in All-Weather Championships Mile which he won last season. Bounce back needed.

Gained reward after promising start for new connections when winning at Southwell in clear-cut fashion. Has held his form on both subsequent starts, looking unlucky not to finish closer when fourth of 14 in All-Weather Championships Mile last time. Turf record is patchy but can figure.

Underperformed during US stint but quickly found top form back in Britain last year, hitting the frame in a trio of top-end handicaps (including Royal Hunt Cup). Lost his way towards the end of last campaign and was too free on return at Doncaster 5 weeks ago. Now has a bit to prove.

Hard to predict but put his best foot forward to resume winning ways with a career-best effort in 12-runner handicap at Lingfield (1m) last month, staying on to lead post. Not certain to back that up returned to turf given overall record.
Registered 3 victories over 7f last year but shaped as if needing the run after 4 months off at Newmarket recently. Cheekpieces reapplied for his first crack at 1m.
4-time winner in France who looks on a good opening mark judged on the pick of that form and has joined a yard that's going well. Could be worth chancing on his first outing for 15 months.
Won two handicaps on turf last year showing useful form. Tailed off on his final couple of starts though (all-weather debut latest), so returns with a bit to prove.

Mostly campaigned at a higher level as a 3-y-o and took advantage of an easier task after 6 months off when winning 6-runner handicap at Southwell (1m) just over 3 weeks ago, adding to a good record when fresh. Task is to now back that up returned to turf.

Proved as good as ever when successful at Newcastle in January and back to his best when ½-length third of 12 to Angel Hunter at Lingfield (1m) last month. All his wins have come on all-weather and he still has plenty to prove on turf.
Started 2025 with 3 AW wins. Ran well when second of 8 at Kempton (1m) back in January and he seems to be building up to something. Does need to prove himself on turf, however.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: HARRY KNOWS was unlucky not to make a winning debut and can make amends at the second time of asking. Rollthedicebaby makes most appeal of the newcomers, with Moriarty Moon also an interesting type on paper.

racers.timeForm: Foaled April 27. 35,000 gns yearling, Starspangledbanner colt. Half-brother to several winners, including useful 6f winner She Do and winner up to 1m Sydney Street. Dam 1m winner. Should make a 2-y-o on paper.
Foaled March 8. €35,000 foal, £32,000 yearling, Lucky Vega colt. Dam 1m winner.

Foaled February 27. €4,000 yearling, Armor filly. Half-sister to several winners, including useful 1m winner Bijin and 10.4f winner Deep State. Irish raider from yard who saddled the 2024 winner, though she appeals as one for the longer term on paper.

Foaled March 20. 3,800 gns foal, 25,000 gns yearling, Belardo colt. Dam, third at 5f at 2 yrs, half-sister to smart winner up to 6f Tis Marvellous. Sales price increased as a yearling and trainer's newcomers command respect. NON RUNNER.

€40,000 yearling, Mehmas colt. Unlucky not to win when head second of 9 in maiden at Newbury (5f, good, 17/2) on debut 14 days ago, conceding first run after hampered start. Yard have made a good start to the turf season and he can put his experience edge to good use here.
Foaled February 8. £38,000 yearling, Soldier's Call filly. Dam 7f winner out of useful 2-y-o 5f winner Mary Read. Looks a likely type on pedigree for a yard who can ready one.
Foaled April 10. 22,000 gns yearling, Dark Angel colt. Half-brother to 7f/1m winner Monfrid. Dam 7f-8.3f winner. Yard won this last year with subsequent Windsor Castle winner Havana Hurricane.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: PATHEIN created a good impression when winning on debut last year and, with further improvement likely this season, is taken to make a winning return. Pacific Avenue arrives fit and looks the main danger if the selection misfires, while Protection Act is also open to progress.

racers.timeForm: Consistent sort who won twice from 5 starts as a juvenile and has already posted creditable efforts when placed in a local Group 2 at Doha and a length second of 9 to Title Role in a listed race at Meydan this year. Lacks the potential of some, but holds a clear fitness advantage.

Won back-to-back 1m novices at Kempton in August and September (posted a useful timefigure under aggressive tactics), before coming unstuck in the 1¼m Zetland Stakes at Newmarket on his final start last year. Drop back in trip should suit, but race conditions are not in his favour.

Looked a good prospect when scoring on debut in a 10-runner maiden at Doncaster in September and improved on that when 1½ lengths fifth of 7 to Hankelow in the Autumn Stakes at Newmarket the following month, briefly looking the winner's chief threat. Sure to progress as a 3-y-o.

Son of Starspangledbanner who looked a useful prospect when winning a 9-runner 7f minor event at Haydock on debut in July, beating Look To The Stars by a length. Not seen since, but open to improvement on his return.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: A useful sprint. Robert Cowell pair LEXINGTON BLITZ and Rhythm N Hooves arrive on the back of decent efforts at Musselburgh over Easter. The former was bang there from the off and gave best only towards the finish in that competitive race and is taken to resume winning ways now. Tropical Storm was behind the Cowell duo in that same Musselburgh contest but left the impression the outing will bring him on. King of Light could also have a say if fully primed for his first start since the autumn.

racers.timeForm: Dual winner on heavy ground for Peter Chapple-Hyam as a juvenile in 2023. Three wins in Europe last year, including a Milan listed, suggest he's still very useful ahead of this return to Britain for a new trainer.  Has been gelded.

Consistent sort (third in last year's Portland) but this regular slow starter doesn't have a great strike-rate (2-22). Should come on for his Newmarket reappearance 17 days ago but others are stronger for the win again.

Three wins in 2025, the latest at Newbury (5f, good to firm) off 1 lb higher in August. Respectable efforts in his 3 outings this year, with the ground softer than he ideally wants it when fifth (reopposing stablemate Lexington Blitz third) of 14 at Musselburgh 27 days ago. Enters calculations.

Enthusiastic front-runner who proved better than ever when easy winner of 5f handicap at Haydock (good to firm) last autumn. Good third in 5f Lingfield listed event (all-weather) on reappearance and possibly unsuited by testing ground when down the field at Musselburgh since.

Back to winning ways at Catterick (5f, good to soft) last autumn. Cracking reappearance effort when third of 14 at Musselburgh (5f, soft) 27 days ago, in the firing line throughout. All ground comes alike to him. Should go well again.
Has thrived on all-weather in recent starts, completing a hat-trick last autumn and posting good runner-up efforts on his last 3 outings. Needs to prove he's equally as effective on turf now.

Listed winner at York over 5f last May. Lost his way subsequently but his mark has come down as a result and he should be sharper for last month's Musselburgh reappearance (not helped by being hampered at the start).

Smart gelding who was a 4-time winner in 2025, signing off with a Group 3 success at Dundalk in October, but has failed to fire in 4 outings this year. Needs a change of headgear (cheekpieces for blinkers) to help spark a revival.

Did well last year, notably a win in a York Ebor meeting handicap (5.4f, good to firm) in August. Possibly unsuited by softer ground when down the field in the Portland at Doncaster on final start. Much depends on whether he's fully tuned after 7 months off.

Useful form in the US earlier in his career. Limited impact in 3 outings for Joseph O'Brien in Ireland last year and hard to know how much he achieved when going close twice at Saint Moritz for Olly Murphy in February. Looks on a tough mark starting out for Richard Hannon.

Really found form in a cheekpieces and tongue tie combination for Stuart Williams last autumn, winning 5f Haydock handicap before creditable fourth of 11 at Ascot (5f, soft). There could be more to come in 2026 if he can sharpen up his starts.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: There's no guarantee that this pans out ideally for CREPE SUZETTE, though her class may see her through, regardless. Coedana went the right way last season and could progress again, while Ryka has proven herself in this grade and is entitled to be competitive under a penalty.

racers.timeForm: Well held in a similar event at Lingfield on final start for Tom Ward in November. Subsequently sold for 70,000 gns and while she has a fine course record, her limitations in this grade have been exposed.

Crystal Ocean filly (bred for stamina) who was ridden positively when a game winner over 1¼m on debut at Leicester in September. The third has franked that form, and while this is a much tougher test, she's open to improvement upped in distance.

Placed in a listed race over 1¼m here last season but didn't go with the same fluency in a Newmarket handicap (1¾m) on her latest start in August. May benefit from a return to more positive tactics, though, particularly given the likely pace scenario here.

Looked most progressive when making it 2-2 in handicaps on the all-weather last September and still looked in rude health when undone by the longer trip when third at Haydock (1¾m) the following month. She's well worth her place in listed company and there could be more to come.
Fair bumper winner hails from a good middle-distance staying family, and she made a successful start on the Flat at Kempton in late-March. Open to improvement but this is a marked step up in class.

Hails from a family her yard know knows well, and she proved progressive in handicaps last season, looking unlucky not to land a hat-trick at Newmarket in October. Came up well short upped to Group 3 company in testing conditions at Newbury later that month, though.

Matched her best form when runner-up in a C&D handicap last summer and while she proved as good as ever when filling the same position on her return (following a breathing operation) at Kempton, the step up to listed company is probably a bridge too far.

Very much on the up at the end of last season, doing all her best work late when third in the Group 2 Park Hill at Doncaster (14.5f). There's a possibility she could prove vulnerable back down in trip, if this becomes tactical, but she still sets a clear standard.

Enhanced her excellent strike rate when winning a listed race at Toulouse (1½m) with a bit in hand last October. She's a strong stayer at this trip, though, and may not be seen to best effect if the pace is steady.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: This has the feel of a competitive handicap, though EVENING SAIGON is by far the least exposed, and he can defy a 3 lb rise for his recent Newcastle win. Diligently is feared most back down in grade, while Far Above Dream is respected in his bid to make it 3-3 over C&D.

racers.timeForm: Beverley debut winner who ran poorly in a valuable sales race on final start for Richard Fahey in September 2024. Subsequently sold for 17,000 gns and has been gelded ahead of this first start for 19 months.

Having fallen down the weights for Richard Fahey last year, he ran well when a very well-supported second on stable debut at Lingfield (all-weather), and a similar performance should see him in the mix again.
Won 4 times in 2025 and opened his account for this year at the first time of asking at Wolverhampton in early-February. Up 2 lb but cannot be discounted given his record at this track.
Made it 2-2 over this C&D when successful in a slightly higher grade here in October, showing a willing attitude, and another good account is expected off a 2 lb higher mark.
Finished last season in fine heart, going close twice in lesser company at Bath, though she's probably vulnerable in this grade on her return.

Low-mileage 4-y-o showed himself a sprinter still on the up when making a winning return at Newcastle last time, always having things pretty much under control, and he makes plenty of appeal in his bid to follow up.

Extended a long losing run for Darryll Holland last year, though ran respectably behind a well-backed winner at Leicester on stable debut/reappearance, and he's 5 lb lower than when second in this race 12 months ago.

Won twice over 6f last year, latterly in a fairly useful handicap at Salisbury, but he looked rusty on reappearance/first start since a gelding operation at Lingfield last time. Entitled to come on for that, though.

Backed up a useful Windsor success when chasing home a subsequent winner at Thirsk on final start last season and there were plenty of positives in his reappearance fourth at Newmarket. Should make a bold bid back down in grade.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: It's unlikely that a 6 lb rise will be enough to prevent LUX AETERNA adding to last month's Wolverhampton win, provided that he proves equally effective on turf. Veritable has been handed a reasonable mark for this handicap debut and he is next on the list ahead of Bridge of Eagles, while Morbeh is also likely to be on the premises.

racers.timeForm: Showed ability in 3 starts at around 1m as a juvenile and, gelded during the winter, he can be expected to improve now upped in trip for this handicap debut.
Fair maiden who has made the frame in all but one of her 8 starts. However, she continues to look vulnerable for win purposes and needs to raise her game now pitched into a handicap.

Twice a runner-up in all-weather novices at Lingfield but went too freely on his first go in handicap company there in January. Settled better in a first-time hood (retained) at Bath (1m, good to soft) and not without each-way hope now upped in trip.
Reached the frame in maidens at Lingfield and Wolverhampton in December. Improved when making a winning handicap debut at Nottingham (8.3f, good to soft) last month but this looks tougher up 5 lb.

Just minor promise in 3 runs at 2 yrs but gelded during the winter and duly improved when striking on first run in a handicap at Wolverhampton (9.5f). 6 lb rise for that impressive display is fair enough and he should have more to offer.

Gradual progress with each of his 3 starts at 2 yrs, last seen chasing home a highly promising and unbeaten Godolphin colt at Kempton (11f) in December. Gelded since and he's one to consider now handicapping.

Proved a different proposition when successful on handicap debut upped to 1¼m at Lingfield in January. Creditable fourth of 8 off this 5 lb higher mark on turf next time and will be a threat if the first-time cheekpieces help eke out a little more.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: DIAMOND BAY is attractively handicapped on his success in this race 12 months ago and he gets the vote. Gallivanted makes appeal on just his second start in a handicap, having gone close at Thirsk last time, while Market House can continue his fine run of form on return to the Flat.

racers.timeForm: Has been a fine servant since joining James Owen, winning his sole turf Flat start for the yard at Brighton last May and notching a second career hurdles victory at Plumpton last month. Should give his running back on the level, with cheekpieces replacing a visor.
Won a staying handicap on the all-weather last autumn and while he should be fit following a spin over hurdles at Ludlow in late-March, this represents a step up in grade on return to the Flat.

Won a fair Kempton maiden (12f) on final start for Tom Clover last season, and following a productive season over hurdles for his new yard, ran well when close third in a similar event on handicap debut at Thirsk. He's the least exposed runner in this field and needs considering.

Made most when successful in this grade at Sandown last season and while he returns to the Flat following a very consistent juvenile campaign over hurdles, he doesn't look to have much in hand from his current mark.

No show in a couple of all-weather starts this year but quickly finds himself on a 6 lb lower mark than when winning this race on reappearance in 2025, and he's fancied to bounce back in a change of headgear.
Landed a double in this grade at Salisbury last autumn, and while probably needing his all-weather reappearance last time, he does look a shade high in the weights.
Underlined a poor record on the Flat for current yard when trailing the field at Bath last time.

Won twice on the turf course at Lingfield under this good-value apprentice last summer and while best not judged on her final run of the season at Newbury in October, she does have a bit to find at the weights on her return.

Went close at Bath on stable debut last autumn and ran to a similar level when fifth in a competitive 14-runner handicap at Newbury (1¼m) on second start this season. Has stamina to prove over this markedly longer trip, though.

Runner-up over this trip on stable debut at Wolverhampton in December but failed to improve upped to 2m at Kempton the following month. Another absence suggests he's probably not been the easiest to train nowadays.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: Ian McCarthy won the hunter here on Tuesday and prolific point scorer HEARTS AND SPADES is taken to provide him with a second straight win in this on the back of his promising debut in this sphere at Cork last month. Gordon Elliott's Last Round can bounce back from a lesser run at Naas in February and give the selection most to think about ahead of last year's runner-up Squire Ohara.

racers.timeForm: Poor maiden hurdler last year and has made only a minor impact in 3 points since. First-time cheekpieces need to spark major improvement.
Poor maiden hurdler/chaser (pulled up in this race last year). Won points at the start of her career but has struggled in more recent times.
Won a maiden point last March but has found life tougher this spring. Tongue tied for his hunter chase debut.

Fair maiden hurdler for Colm Murphy in 2024. Prolific in the pointing field for this yard since and made an encouraging start to his hunter career when third of 16 at Cork (3m, soft) last month, a late mistake proving costly. Major player for last year's winning stable.

Runner-up in this 12 months ago and not disgraced in a good hunter at Down Royal over Christmas on his first outing for this yard. Unable to make an impact in points since but dangerous to rule out a revival given his fine effort last year.
Pulled up in bumper for Willie Mullins in autumn 2024 but has fared better in the pointing field since, winning a 3m maiden last month. Hunter debut.
Made it sixth time lucky in points at the end of March but more will be needed if he's to follow up on hunter debut.
Just a modest maiden hurdler for this top yard but did win a small-field maiden point 12 days ahead of this hunter chase debut.

Represents a top yard and easily landed 14-runner maiden hunter at Limerick (22.5f, heavy) over Christmas. Good third of 13 in a stronger race at Thurles (25f, good to soft) in January. Latest remote fourth at Naas was disappointing but capable of bouncing back after break.
Won 2 hunter chases at Downpatrick last spring. Placed twice in points this year but pulled up in a hunter at Fairyhouse over Easter. First-time blinkers replace regular cheekpieces.
One win from 67 starts under Rules. Should be sharper for a point run last month but would still rate a surprise winner.
Beaten 25 lengths when second in a maiden point last month and pulled up in both hunters. Outsider.
Unplaced on his completed start in points and big outsider on hunter debut.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: The vote goes to LETS GO CHAMP, who was a winner of a major handicap at this meeting in 2024 and he has made a very positive start in hunters, seeing off Hunters Yarn at Gowran in March before giving it a good shot when runner-up in the Foxhunters' at Aintree. Panda Boy and Its On The Line, fifth and ninth respectively at Aintree, rate the main dangers. The last-named is bidding for a fourth win in a row in this race but Panda Boy is feared most. Wonderwall also enters calculations.

racers.timeForm: Winner of 4 of her 5 starts in points and also struck on hunter debut at Down Royal in March. Should have more to offer given her low mileage but this demands a significant step forward.

Dual hurdles winner for Willie Mullins has done well since joining present yard, winning 2 of his 3 starts between the flags in February/March, Fine second on hunter debut at Cork (2½m, soft) last month and he's a strong each-way candidate.

Useful bumper/fairly useful hurdle winner for Paul Nicholls and, having won 2 of his 3 starts in points during the winter, he was still bang there when falling 3 out in the Fairyhouse hunter won by Five Star Getaway. Successful between the flags again since and he remains open to improvement.

Most likeable and dependable hunter chaser who has won the last 3 running of this. Runner-up in the Cheltenham Festival hunter for third year in a row in March before finishing ninth of 24 in the Aintree Foxhunters' over what is probably now an inadequate trip (21f) for this 9-y-o. Leading claims.
Fairly useful hunter chaser in 2024/25 but pulled up in this race 12 months ago and has also failed to complete in 3 of his subsequent half-a-dozen appearances.
Unreliable sort who was beaten a long way in the Fairyhouse hunter won by Five Star Getaway last month.

Useful chaser for Henry de Bromhead who won an open point in February before making a successful return to Rules in a 25f Gowran hunter the following month, proving a neck too strong for Hunters Yarn. Solid second in the Aintree Foxhunters' last time and another bold show anticipated.
Point winner in February and made it third time lucky in hunters when landing a maiden in decisive fashion at Downpatrick (3m, soft). Remains open to improvement.
In good heart between the flags during the past 12 months and made a winning hunter debut back under Rules at Fairyhouse (25f, soft) last time, left clear 2 out. However, much more on his plate here.

Delivered assured rounds of jumping when winning first 2 starts in this sphere. Didn't see things out as well as anticipated having belted the third last when fifth of 23 at the Cheltenham Festival in March, but solid claims here nonetheless. Visor applied.

Winner of the big Cheltenham Festival hunter last spring. Only seventh in this season's renewal of that race but he was given a lot to do that day and has since demonstrated his wellbeing with a decisive display between the flags. Key player.
Fairly useful chaser at best but hasn't made much of an impact switched to hunters on his last 2 starts under Rules.

Smart for Willie Mullins in his prime and, having found just one too good on first 2 starts in hunters for this yard, he looked poised to deliver the goods when falling 3 out in the race won by Five Star Getaway at Fairyhouse last month.
Good second in 25f Roscommon handicap chase last June but failed to complete next 2 starts and well held on the latest of his 2 starts between the flags in March. Opposable on hunter debut.

Good third of 29 in the Aintree Foxhunters' last spring and was second to Its On The Line in the 2024 renewal of this race. Point winner during the winter but he was comprehensively outpointed by Panda Boy at Thurles in January (also behind Wonderwall between the flags last time).

raceEventDetails.timeForm: The admirable DINOBLUE is unbeaten in her last 6 starts in mares company, making it back-to-back wins in the Mrs Paddy Power Mares' Chase at Cheltenham last time, and she can also land this race for the second year running. Only By Night was runner-up to Dinoblue at Cheltenham and could be the chief threat again, with Kala Conti completing the shortlist.

racers.timeForm: Winning hurdler who showed better form when making the frame on first 4 starts over fences, including when runner-up in mares handicap here (2¾m) in February. However, below par the last twice and looks up against it at this level.

Made bright start over fences when winning first 2 races, including Grade 2 mares novice at Cork in December. Progress has stalled at the highest level the last twice, though likely to have been involved in the finish but for falling 3 out in the Maghull at Aintree. Could bounce back.

Won first 3 starts over fences last season before runner-up at the highest level at Cheltenham and this meeting. Successful in Grade 3 at Naas in November and bounced back from a lesser effort when second to Dinoblue at Cheltenham last time. Can give another good account.

Yet to add to her chasing debut success but was a good second on stable debut in handicap at Thurles in February. Also ran well when second in 3-runner Grade 3 at Cork last time, but faces a tough ask in this contest.

Much improved over fences, winning Grade 1 against the males at Fairyhouse last season and making it 5 wins on the spin at Doncaster in December. Pulled up in Irish Gold Cup next time, before not discredited conceding weight all round when fourth behind Dinoblue at Cheltenham.

Landed the Mrs Paddy Power Mares' Chase at Cheltenham in 2025 before a wide-margin winner of this race. Runner-up against the males after a break but has won all 3 starts in mares company since, comfortably seeing off Only By Night back at Cheltenham last time. Leading contender.

gameStateTimeScore.gameEventComments: We are paying 5 PLACES instead of 4 at 1/5 odds (min 16). BOG does not apply to Each Way bets. T&C's apply.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: FUNICULI FUNICULA is one of 8 for Willie Mullins, but unlike some of his stablemates he arrives unexposed and on the back of a light campaign. Paul Townend's decision to ride him over the yard's other runners looks significant and a bold bid is expected. Shuffle The Deck is another open to improvement and may prove the main danger, while Noble Park, Kiss Will, Spread Boss Ted and Raglan Road are also respected in an ultra-competitive handicap.

racers.timeForm: Lightly-raced sort who confirmed the promise of his 2 outings in maiden chases when landing the odds at Cork (by ¾ length from Wingmen) earlier this month. Remains open to improvement on handicap debut and another bold show looks likely. The choice of Paul Townend.

Matched useful hurdling form when winning a Galway maiden and Grade 3 novice at Cork on first 2 starts over fences, but has been below that level in 2 runs since, with his jumping letting him down in a valuable Cheltenham handicap last time. A good-value conditional booked but needs to bounce back.

Progressive novice who jumps well and has won 3 of his 5 starts over fences, including an 8-runner handicap chase at Newbury by 4¼ lengths from Rodney. Up 9 lb, but that form has worked out extremely well and could play a leading role if taking to the environment of a large-field handicap.
Useful chaser placed all 4 starts in maidens but well held in the Golden Miller at Cheltenham in March on sole handicap outing. Chased home Funiculi Funicula at Cork on latest outing 26 days ago.

Matched the pick of his hurdling form when winning a 7-runner novice chase at Naas (2½m, soft) 54 days ago by ½ length from Ballygunner Castle, looking suited by the strong pace. Lacks the experience of the hustle and bustle of a large-field handicap, but remains unexposed over fences.

Very useful hurdler at his best who took a step back in the right direction when eighth of 24 in the Martin Pipe at Cheltenham 49 days ago. Has not pulled up any trees in 3 previous chase starts, but is well treated on hurdling form if able to find improvement. Engaged 4.15 here Thursday.

Landed gamble in Catterick handicap hurdle on return and then advanced his form over fences, off the mark at the second attempt when dictating at Sandown last month. Let down by jumping last time, though, and will find it difficult to dominate this much larger field.

Has improved of late, winning handicap chases at Sandown in January (novice event) and March, the latter by 4½ lengths from Toothless. Clearly open to further progress, and his yard has successfully raided this meeting in the past, though he has yet to face anything like this large-field scenario.

Took his form up another notch when making the most of a good opportunity in a 4-runner novice chase at Wexford (25f, heavy) 45 days ago, but faces a completely different test back down in trip and switched to a handicap of this nature. Up against it.

Lightly-raced chaser who made a perfect start over fences when winning a Fairyhouse maiden in January, but has failed to build on that in 2 small-field novices since (beaten by Raglan Road in latter). Needs to produce more than he has shown so far to get involved.

Has taken fairly well to chasing this season, getting off the mark at the fourth attempt when winning 4-runner handicap at Kelso by 2 lengths from Scarlet Jet. Only 2 lb higher here but faces a much more competitive scenario. Cheekpieces on first time.

Useful handicap hurdler who bettered that form over fences when second in the Golden Miller at the Cheltenham Festival in 2024/25, before winning a Kilbeggan maiden in June. Stretched by 3m trip since, including back over hurdles. Tongue tie back on with Kennedy in the saddle but progress needed.

Stepped up markedly from chasing debut when seeing off 7 rivals in a Fairyhouse maiden (17f, soft) in January and backed that up when 5¾ lengths third of 5 to Jacob's Ladder in the Flyingbolt at Navan 62 days ago. Step back up in trip will suit, but more needed on handicap debut.
Useful hurdler and easily best effort over fences when third of 12 to Goraibhmaithagat in handicap chase at Naas (heavy) 43 days ago. Cheekpieces on first time. RESERVE.

Promising type who again caught the eye over fences when 11-length third of 12 to Come Walk With Me in a handicap chase at Fairyhouse earlier this month. The second has won off a similar mark since, and any further progress is likely to see him involved at the finish.

Belatedly matched his fairly useful hurdling form over fences when winning a 7-runner novice chase at Down Royal 45 days ago by ½ length from Slanagaibhgoleir. Harry Cobden now takes the ride and, now up and running, he may have more to offer, with any market support worth serious note.

Useful sort who ran creditably when sixth of 22 to Wellington Arch in a valuable handicap hurdle at Aintree last time. Yet to win in 3 chase starts, finishing second in small-field maidens on his first 2 attempts before running down the field in a Musselburgh handicap. Progress required.

Has quickly developed into a smart maiden chaser and looked the main threat to Soldier in Milan when departing at the third-last in the Irish Grand National 25 days ago. Marked drop in trip shouldn't be a problem and obvious claims if none the worse for that fall, but Townend prefers stablemate.

Won a conditional handicap chase at Leopardstown in December and got back on track when a 1¾-length second of 12 to Showurappreciation under this rider in a novice handicap at Navan (3m, soft) 41 days ago. The winner has advertised the form since, but the drop back in trip is a slight concern.

Useful hurdler who has run to a similar level when runner-up on both completed starts in maiden chases, latterly beaten ½ length by Spread Boss Ted at Naas in March. Will need to step up on that form if he is to make an impact on handicap debut.

Yet to come close to matching hurdles form over fences and, while he's shaped as if having a bigger performance in him as chaser, his jumping left a lost to be desired last time. Difficult to make a case for. RESERVE.

Won a Clonmel maiden chase in December and has held his form in varied events since, including when a creditable fifth of 12 in a handicap chase at Naas (2½m, heavy) 68 days ago. This is likely too competitive, however.

Off the mark in this sphere at Wexford last summer and posted his best effort yet when finding only Ol Man Dingle too good in a Cork Grade 3 novice in November. Below that level in valuable handicaps and Grade 3 novice at Limerick (½-length second of 4 to Uhavemeinstitches) since, however.

Left her first 2 chase runs behind when easily winning a 9-runner maiden at Thurles in March and caught the eye with how smoothly she travelled when fourth of 12 to Come Walk With Me in a listed novice handicap at Fairyhouse last time. This is tougher, though, and others are preferred back at 2½m.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: The tight grip held on this race by Willie Mullins in recent years looks set to continue with KING RASKO GREY's claims hard to ignore on the back of his decisive Cheltenham Festival success. Kiely's Place, one of 4 stablemates, is pretty promising and he gets the nod ahead of the 4-y-o Lord Byron for forecast purposes.

racers.timeForm: Successful on the second of 2 outings in points and while his pedigree is far from flashy, there was plenty to like about his hurdle debut success at Clonmel in February. Came up short in a Fairyhouse Grade 2 next time but he remains capable of better. Hood applied.

Half-brother to yard's high-class jumper Saint Roi and made a winning Irish debut in a 2m Navan maiden hurdle in December. Has found life tougher in better company since, though, and King Rasko Grey is clearly the stable No 1.

Confirmed the promise of her debut when landing a Down Royal bumper last spring and successful first 2 starts in this sphere. Wasn't disgraced in the Grade 2 mares novice hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival last time and not without each-way hope upped in trip here.
Looked a useful prospect when making a successful hurdles debut at Limerick in December but struggled in a Grade 2 at Fairyhouse since. Tongue tie goes on and a big step forward is needed.
Belatedly matched useful bumper form when winning Monksfield Novices' Hurdle at Naas in November. Wasn't beaten far when third of 5 back there last time but he looks vulnerable at this level.

Made it 2-3 in this sphere and took a step forward in the process when landing a Grade 3 novice at Thurles (21f, heavy) in February. However, he is very much in the shadow of stablemate King Rasko Grey here.

Runner-up on second of 2 Flat starts for Aidan O'Brien. Yet to hit the target in 5 outings in this sphere but has acquitted himself well on each occasion, including in Grade 1s at the big Cheltenham and Aintree festivals. Place possibilities.

Made the frame both starts in bumpers here and has quickly made up into a smart novice hurdler, asserting in good style when landing the Turners at the Cheltenham Festival (21f, good) in March. Hard to oppose.

One of the leading bumper performers of the 2023/24 season who cemented positive start since returning from a lengthy absence when opening hurdles account at Naas in February. However, he was out with the washing in the Albert Bartlett at the Cheltenham Festival next time.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: LOSSIEMOUTH quickly left behind a rare below-par effort when landing the Champion Hurdle at Cheltenham in good style and she can add another Grade 1 success to her remarkable CV. The main danger could be William Munny, who has a lengthy absence to overcome but had developed into a very smart novice, ahead of Golden Ace.

racers.timeForm: Has developed into a smart performer this season, registering a first graded success in the Limestone Lad at Naas in January. However, found things tougher next time when down the field in a Grade 2 at Fairyhouse 25 days ago.

Runner-up in listed handicap here last year and has continued to go the right way this season, recording major handicap successes at Ascot in December (form worked out well) and in the County at Cheltenham. Up in grade but he's worth a chance at this level.

Smart Flat performer who proved better than ever in this sphere when winning Sussex Champion Hurdle at Plumpton a year ago. Well below his best in 2 starts back over hurdles this spring, though was closing when making a mistake at the last in minor event at Cork 26 days ago.

Looked an exciting prospect when winning first 4 starts, including a pair of Grade 3s on first 2 outings for Willie Mullins in 2024/25. However, hasn't been able to kick on at the highest level this season, bad mistake at the second in the Champion Hurdle at Cheltenham last time.

Credit to connections, landing a second Cheltenham Festival success in the 2025 Champion Hurdle, albeit fortunate. Again had things go her way when scoring in the Fighting Fifth at Newcastle, before running creditably in defeat last 3 starts. Can go well with cheekpieces added.

Winner of 14 of her 17 completed starts, including victories in the Mares Champion Hurdle and Morgiana at this course. Fitted with cheekpieces, recorded her fourth Cheltenham Festival success in the Champion Hurdle last time, scoring with plenty in hand, and she's the one to beat.

Smart form in bumpers and progressive over hurdles in 2024/25, opening account with an impressive success in listed novice over this C&D. In first-time hood, excellent second to Kopek des Bordes in the Supreme at Cheltenham when last seen and he's respected despite his 13-month absence.
