raceEventDetails.timeForm: CHICHESTER PARK is taken to make it back-to-back successes in this race for the Tony Martin yard. Unexposed High Court Cave is one of many dangers in a wide-open renewal, along with handicap debutante In My Teens, who could prove well treated on her Flat form.

racers.timeForm: Went backwards in this sphere following a winning hurdle debut at Navan last spring. Has since left M. D. O'Callaghan and faces an uphill task at the weights on handicap/stable debut.
Decisive winner of a Downpatrick handicap hurdle last July but returns in blinkers, following a laboured effort in a handicap chase there the following month.

€180,000 point recruit who made the most of a good opportunity in a Thurles maiden in March but wasn't seen to anything like best effect when seventh of 21 on handicap debut at Fairyhouse. This should play out more favourably, and he's well worth another chance.

Dual winner around 2m in maiden/novice company but turned in a rare poor effort over hurdles when well beaten at Fairyhouse last time. Likely to come up short, even if refitted cheekpieces have the desired effect.

Free-going sort readily opened her hurdles account at the second time of asking and reproduced that form when runner-up in a Naas novice last November. The switch to a big-field handicap ought to suit and she could be capable of even better.

Solid fourth in a listed handicap hurdle at Listowel last season and was clearly in fine heart when ending a long losing run on the Flat at Dundalk in December. Worth considering back over jumps, especially if supported.

Made it back-to-back handicaps in heavy ground at Fairyhouse in February and resumed progress when third in a fairly useful handicap at Clonmel (soft) on his latest start. Likely to face less-testing conditions here but does arrive with a positive profile.

Crystal Ocean mare ran out a decisive winner in a first-time hood at Limerick in February. Well held in a competitive race on her handicap bow at Fairyhouse subsequently, but she's surely better than that. Headgear goes back on.

Successful on handicap hurdle debut at Leopardstown in early-March and confirmed that improvement when runner-up on first start over fences at Downpatrick. She's low mileage and cannot be discounted with tongue strap back on for hurdles return.

Has been going through the motions over hurdles since running a stormer to finish fourth in a competitive handicap at the Galway Festival last summer, but at least merits a market check given who trains him.

Had excuses in bumpers prior to making a successful hurdling debut at Downpatrick and is best not judged on his final start for Gavin Cromwell in a Grade 3 last November. May do better now sent handicapping by new yard.

Has remained in good form since opening his account at Thurles in December, and having been far from ideally placed when eighth of 19 on handicap debut at Down Royal in March, he's fancied to do better for yard who won this race 12 months ago.

Again wasn't seen to best effect in this sphere when third of 5 in a Fairyhouse novice on latest hurdle start, but he should find this run to suit and makes each-way appeal on the back of a pipe-opener at the Curragh last time.

Fairly useful French juvenile hurdle winner who defied market expectations and a 28-month absence to make a winning stable/British debut at Newbury 2m in March, picking up well to lead in the dying strides. He's been given time to get over those exertions and could progress again.

Justified support when making the most of a good opportunity in a Wetherby maiden in late-March. Could be interesting now sent handicapping by yard who did well at this Festival last year and have enjoyed some notable handicap success this season.
Held her form well for most of last year, winning twice over this trip, but she clearly wasn't over her Cheltenham fall when trailing the field at Navan in November. RESERVE.
French bumper winner hasn't stood much racing and proved no more tractable for the fitting of a first-time tongue strap when down the field on handicap bow at Fairyhouse.

Handicap debutant is potentially well treated on the form of his Bellewstown maiden win in July 2024, though there wasn't enough encouragement in his comeback run on the Flat to make him of serious interest.
Out of sorts in this sphere last year and it's hard to be confident on the back of a below-part effort on the Flat at Leopardstown 3 weeks ago. RESERVE.

Point/bumper winner who finished second in a competitive 20-runner race at the Galway Festival (2¾m) prior to landing the odds in a Downpatrick (2¼m) maiden last September, and he's very much unexposed on just his second start in handicap company.

Debut bumper winner posted a fairly useful effort when fifth in a novice hurdle at Naas last season and likely needed the run following 13 months off at Fairyhouse in early-April. Cannot be totally discounted with cheekpieces added on just his second handicap start.
Landed the second leg of a double here last season but things clearly haven't gone to plan since falling at Naas this time last year.

Strong-travelling sort had been knocking on the door in handicaps before finishing well beaten under softer conditions at Cheltenham in November. He should find this a much more suitable test and isn't ruled out if ready to roll.
Useful Flat performer hasn't built on a promising hurdle debut but is the type to do better now handicapping, her mark potentially a lenient one given her ability on the level.

Likeable mare shaped with promise in a pair of handicaps here last winter and posted another creditable effort when third in a mares handicap at Bellewstown last time. No surprise to see her in the mix again.
Went close on a couple of occasions last year, and having likely needed the run in the Sussex Champion Hurdle at Plumpton on his latest start, he's entitled to be in the mix if lining up. RESERVE.

Has been in fine form following the application of cheekpieces, finishing third in a mares listed handicap on her latest hurdles start, prior to a pair of fairly useful placed efforts on the Flat last month.

Hasn't kicked on from a breakthrough success over hurdles at Listowel, though wasn't ideally placed on her latest hurdle start and was probably having a pipe-opener on her return to the Flat last time. Yard also saddle Chichester Park.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: CITYOFBLINDINLITES was unlucky to bump into subsequent Champion Bumper winner The Mourne Rambler on his debut at Leopardstown in December and, with the longer trip likely to be within range, he looks the one to beat. Premier Division was only 2¼ lengths behind the selection in the aforementioned race and must be taken seriously, while Largy Star and Ladbroke Grove are others to consider.

racers.timeForm: Dual point winner who showed plenty to work on behind a promising one at Naas on bumper debut (19f) in January. Again shaped promisingly sent hurdling in a first-time tongue strap when third of 25 at Fairyhouse (2½m) 9 weeks later and has solid each-way claims back in this code.

€110,000 3-y-o, Walk In The Park gelding. Closely related to useful 2m hurdle winner Sporting Glory, stays 25f, and half-brother to 2 winners, including useful chaser The Flier Begley. Runner-up on last of 3 starts in points and the market should offer up some clues ahead of this switch to Rules.

Walk In The Park gelding who has shaped with plenty of promise on both bumper outings, including when third to subsequent Champion Bumper winner The Mourne Rambler at Leopardstown (2m) on latest start. Has a bit of ground to make up with Cityofblindinlites but big chance otherwise.

Improved appreciably on his debut form when second of 9 in bumper at Leopardstown (2½m, good) in December. Left Brian M. McMahon after and matched that form when filling same spot at Limerick 4 months later.
Won sole start in British points but was very green and well held in Fairyhouse bumper on debut in November.

Didn't show a great deal on first 2 outings in bumpers but improved appreciably on hurdling debut form when runner-up in 18-runner maiden at Fairyhouse (2½m) on New Year's Day. Shaped better than the distance beaten suggests back in this code at Gowran since but hard to fancy in this company.
Has shaped with some promise in a Leopardstown maiden hurdle and when third of 16 in a Cork bumper (19f). Needs more for win purposes, however.
Austrian School gelding. Dam unraced half-sister to useful hurdler/chaser (stayed 3¼m) Bally Longford.

Wings of Eagles gelding. Half-brother to bumper winner/fairly useful hurdler Ballymountain Boy, stayed 3m. Looked one for the longer term when finishing down the field at Down Royal on his debut in December.

Vadamos gelding who showed plenty starting out in a hood and tongue strap combination when second to subsequent Champion Bumper winner The Mourne Rambler at Leopardstown (2m) in December. Should stay this longer trip and has to be considered the one to beat.
Falco gelding who exceeded expectations to some tune (66/1) when third in 9-runner bumper at Clonmel (2½m, soft) on last month's debut. Remains to be seen if he's able to build on that.
Mahler gelding. Dam (h112) 2m-21f hurdle winner.
Little promise in a trio of starts in this sphere prior to unseating her rider early on her Tramore hurdling debut.

£185,000 purchase after easily landed sole outing in points and shaped encouragingly under a positive ride when second of 12 in 2m Thurles bumper in February. Not quite in same form when ridden with more restraint in a similar event there the following month.

€74,000 Beaumec de Houelle gelding who showed plenty setting out in a tongue strap when third of 20 in 2m bumper at this meeting a year earlier. Not seen since but that form has worked out well and he's likely to improve.
Jukebox Jury gelding who made an unpromising start to his career when beating only one home in a bumper at Down Royal (17f) on Boxing Day. Has left C. Moore.
Steady progress in 4 runs last year, albeit possibly flattered in a steadily-run listed event at Gowran when last seen. Up against it.

Soldier of Fortune gelding who ran to a fair level when third of 11 in bumper at this course 2½ years ago on sole outing for R. P. Cody. Since transferred to Willie Mullins and promises to be suited by the longer trip on pedigree.

Successful on sole outing in points (beat a good prospect) but hasn't quite lived up to market expectations on both bumper starts, going in snatches when third of 4 at this course (2m) on most recent outing. Up in trip.

A 6-figure store from a very good jumping family who showed promise setting out in a tongue strap (already had a breathing operation too) when fourth of 9 at Wetherby in February last year. Raced freely when well beaten at this meeting on only outing since. Has left Fergal O'Brien.

Walk In The Park gelding. Brother to fair 21f hurdle winner Dramatic Encore. Dam (h132), bumper/2m hurdle winner, half-sister to smart hurdler/chaser who later became temperamental Bright New Dawn (stayed 3m). Third on first of 2 starts in points but last of 4 finishers on latest.
Crystal Ocean mare. Half-sister to numerous winners, including smart hurdler/top-class chaser Don Poli and smart hurdler/useful chaser Debece. Appeals on paper so well worth a market check.
Went with no encouragement in a maiden hurdle at Gowran on debut in November. Upped in trip and fitted with a first-time hood on this switch to a bumper.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: GREAT VALLEY looked a useful prospect in opening his hunter account at the first time of asking at Ludlow last month and is a straightforward choice to follow up. Franigane is preferred to On Lovers Walk for forecast purposes.

racers.timeForm: Didn't need to improve to win a weak 4-runner hunter chase at Fakenham (3m, good) 18 days ago. value for extra having edged ahead on line under mainly hands-and-heels riding. Faces a stiff task here, however.
Seemingly not the easiest to train but was a good second to Barton Snow in this race last year.

Prolific in points since last seen under Rules for Dan Skelton and made a successful hunter debut in 5-runner event at Ludlow (2½m, good to soft) last month. Rates a useful prospect and this looks an excellent opportunity to follow up.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: THE DANCING TREE has won his previous 5 starts in points and is taken to extend his winning sequence on hunter debut. Practice Run finished ahead of Mister Splash in a point this spring, and Bradley Gibbs' charge is a tentative selection for the forecast.

racers.timeForm: Fair maiden hurdler under Rules and won twice in points last year. Beaten 1½ lengths in a match by very promising Boley Bob on latest start between the flags and cannot be discounted.
Won 3 of 7 starts in points, defeating Tellmesomethingood when last successful in January, and he now makes his first start under Rules having finished runner-up in 4-runner event last time.
Multiple point winner had the run of things when narrowly denied in a 4-runner event on hunter debut at Fakenham last time and this looks a much deeper race.
Dual winning pointer who finished runner-up to The Dancing Tree on his penultimate start before scoring in a 4-runner event last time. Represents a trainer/jockey who does well with this type.

Fair second on penultimate start for Gavin Cromwell in early 2025 and has won his previous 5 starts in points for new connections, including last time in a 4-runner event. The one to beat on his form in that sphere.
Dual winning pointer who finished runner-up in a small-field event last month and is probably the stable second string.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: WHAT A GLANCE can probably be forgiven pulling up at the Cheltenham Festival. A close second to a useful sort in a point prior to that suggests this 11-y-o still retains most of his ability and he might be able to deny Mister Coffey a belated first success over fences.

racers.timeForm: Long-standing maiden over fences. His second in a Cheltenham veterans handicap in November shows he's still very useful but his latest reversal in a 23f Newbury hunter underlines he's not one for maximum faith. This is easier.

Looked very progressive when winning twice in this sphere in 2024 (including this race, run at Cheltenham). Has failed to complete in hunters at Ludlow (fell 4 out) and the Cheltenham Festival (pulled up) this year but a near miss in a point in between suggests most of his ability remains.

Well held in a maiden hurdle on her previous start under Rules in 2022. Has won a couple of points since but has struggled in that sphere this season (pulled up 6 times before tailed-off third latest). Outsider on hunter debut.

Useful hurdler/fairly useful chaser for Fergal O'Brien earlier in his career. Disappointing in a hunter chase at Cheltenham for this stable last May but has won points in recent months ahead of this return to Rules.
Fair hurdler/chaser. Has reached the frame in a couple of hunters this spring but likely to be vulnerable for win purposes again.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: A case can be made for all of these but it's possible the youngest pair will come to the fore, with CORPORAL JACKJONES getting a narrow vote over Crawter, who has won a point since flopping at Exeter in March.

racers.timeForm: Made it third time lucky in hunters at Stratford (21f, soft) in March. Good second to a prolific sort in a point since and the one to beat here.

Brother to smart chaser winner Only By Night and this multiple point winner landed this race last year (at Cheltenham) on his first start under Rules. Disappointing on his return to the hunter field at Exeter in March but has won a point since. The obvious threat to Corporal Jackjones.

Lost his way for Paul Webber but very much revived by current yard, winning 4 points before scoring comfortably on 3m Huntingdon hunter debut last May. Unseated first at Stratford later that month. In good form again in the pointing field this year, winning in March/April (second latest).
Fairly useful form without winning in hunters in recent years. Has won 3 small-field points this spring but might be vulnerable to younger legs back under Rules.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: POLICE ACADEMY's wellbeing isn't in doubt following back-to-back wins between the flags and she is taken to make a successful hunter debut for a yard that enjoys plenty of success in this type of race. Hollywood Harmon and All Loved Up can fill the places.

racers.timeForm: First past the post in a mares handicap chase at Uttoxeter in June (subsequently disqualified owing to a prohibited substance). Winner of 2 of her 3 starts in small-field points for present yard and she's a big player on hunter debut.
Won a Doncaster staying handicap chase for Harry Derham last spring, but no show both starts for Sarah-Jayne Davies late last year and 0-4 between the flags for this yard in recent months.

Dual hurdles winner who was runner-up in hunters at Stratford and Ludlow after undergoing another breathing operation. However, form took a turn for the worse last time and questions to answer with regard to stamina here.

Beaten a fair way when fourth of 8 on first start under Rules for Olive Nicholls at Cheltenham (this corresponding race) last spring, but has won 3 of her 4 starts in points since the turn of the year. Couldn't rule out.

Multiple point winner who broke her duck under Rules in 9-runner maiden hunter at Cartmel (21f, soft) under Pippa Brown last spring. Well held in the Aintree Foxhunters last month but this is a more realistic assignment.
Veteran who has won 11 times between the flags (including 12 days ago), but she was pulled up in an Exeter hunter on latest start under Rules in March.
Notched fourth hurdles success on final run for the O'Neill's at Worcester last summer, but 0-5 in points since and she's opposable on hunter debut.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: It was a pretty competitive hunter chase that JEFFERY'S CROSS bagged at Newbury and, with this stiffer test no problem at all, he is taken to enhance his fine record in this sphere. Peaches And Cream is second choice ahead of Slipway.

racers.timeForm: Form figures in hunter chases read 12211 following a narrow success at Newbury (23f, good) last month. Second in this last year and can go one better.
One-time useful chaser who has hit the target between the flags the last twice. Has undergone a breathing operation since and this veteran could be a factor if his stamina passes the test.
Failed to get competitive on hunter debut here in January but bagged a point on his latest appearance in March and he's dangerous to discount.
On a long losing sequence under Rules, but managed to score between the flags in March (also chased home a promising one last time) and he could have a part to play now venturing into hunter company.

Likeable sort who displayed a willing attitude when adding to his tally over fences at Worcester in July and exploited a lower hurdles mark under an attacking ride here in September. However, well held next 2 starts and out of luck in a couple of weak points since.

raceEventDetails.timeForm: Barring accidents UNEXPECTED PARTY should prove too strong for these. He didn't jump/travel with his usual verve at Aintree last time but is now in much calmer waters. Fan de Blues is marginally preferred to Arthur's Sixpence for forecast purposes.

racers.timeForm: Winner of the 2024 Grand Annual at Cheltenham and runner-up in the same race in 2025. Has done well since switched to hunters, scoring at Taunton and Haydock prior to finishing fourth in the 24-runner Foxhunters' at Aintree where he reportedly bled. Hard to oppose on these terms.
Smart handicap chaser for Willie Mullins in 2022/23. Has shown he still retains a fair level of ability for his new yard and he's another with realistic place claims.

Fairly useful hurdle/chase winner at his best and he was a creditable third of 10 in an Exeter handicap chase on final run for Tom Symonds. Winner of one of his 2 starts between the flags since but he's opposable now pitched into a hunter.

Won twice between the flags for Georgina Nicholls last year and performed well above market expectations when third in the 8-runner Newbury hunter won by Jeffery's Cross in March. Minor place money is a distinct possibility here.
Multiple point winner but yet to win a hunter and others make more appeal.
